items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: "I've heard that name before. ... they say clarinet, Joe Blow."

ctx.x: Apparently that's reviewed on a couple of other pages in the book, which I don't have copy here. "May-June -- May to June, 1933, Fletcher Henderson's Blue Harmony Boys, perhaps a vocal group?" Is that -- do you remember that name?

I've heard that name before. The -- excuse me -- the only conclusion I can arrive at about these different names, you know, in recording, just like Benny Goodman has a contract with a certain record company, and they say clarinet, Joe Blow. You see? So these are the way some of these things, like Red Allen had a contract. So if he

recorded with Fletcher, when they gave the personnel of the band, Fletcher's band, they couldn't use Red Allen. They'd have to say Red Smith or anything, to keep Red from getting in trouble with his contract, all this way, so I know this to be a fact.
